title: Create a confidential property fact pack and redacted public-data workspace
proposal: Gather lease, amendments, parcel/title, rent history, tax basis, debt, insurance, maintenance, environmental and title materials into an access-controlled private folder. Publish only placeholders and aggregate outputs.
why: Most decision-critical facts are property- and owner-specific; neither broad market statistics nor the prompt reveals them.

title: Run a dual-track lease-extension and sale process
proposal: Ask tenant for written extension terms while obtaining confidential, written broker pricing and a third-party valuation range; do not commit to either path until both are comparable on net, risk-adjusted terms.
why: Maintains optionality and reveals the tenant's willingness to pay versus market-clearing sale demand.
status: Proposal only — no tenant contact made

title: Use after-tax cash flows and explicit decision hurdles
proposal: Compare sell-now, sell near expiry, renew then hold, renew then sell, and tenant-default/reletting outcomes. Show gross value, transaction costs, tax range, debt payoff, replacement yield, downside, and liquidity separately.
why: Headline sale price, cap-rate assumptions, or untaxed reinvestment returns are not directly comparable to retained rent and residual value.
status: Proposal only — no model inputs fabricated

title: Add parcel-scale planning, demand, school, and hazard evidence
proposal: Only after location is privately validated, append geography-tagged ACS/trade-area statistics, traffic and competition, school assignments, zoning/permit history, FEMA/CAL FIRE/USGS layers, and written insurance quotes.
why: City/county and metro indicators can be directionally useful but are not local substitutes. Hazard maps have geographic and methodological limitations.

title: Make source freshness, geography, status, and model assumptions visible on each row
proposal: Keep a single data ledger with source URL, retrieval date, period, geography, unit, status, revision/vintage, uncertainty and owner; blank unknown values and expose a separate Flagged for Review list.
why: The repository contains many overlapping workbooks with differing methods and vintage; a reader needs to distinguish observed facts from scenarios and stale claims.
status: Proposal only — dashboard implements this for its own rows

title: Keep all identifying and taxpayer data out of the public Pages site
proposal: Never publish owner name, street address, APN, signatures, contact details, bank/debt account numbers, tax returns, personal basis or identifiable raw lease files. Use generated random IDs and rounded ranges only where disclosure risk is acceptable.
why: A public static site is not an appropriate repository for sensitive documents; no such information is required for the public evidence dashboard.
